profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting between the maintainer of an automated fuzzing/minimization toolkit for logic synthesis tools and the engineer who owns the CI regression farm for the project. Context: after adding support for structural Verilog and tighter in-process oracle integration, the nightly fuzzing campaign flagged run 18427 as a regression against LSOracle/ABC, but the reduced testcase now behaves differently depending on where it is replayed. Agenda: compare what each person believes the failing case is, determine whether the reducer changed the bug or only exposed an environment difference, and decide the next diagnostic step before the next nightly run. Expected outcome: align on a concrete replay plan and decide whether to investigate the parser/import path, the minimizer, or the CI execution setup first.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: Fuzzing for EDA tools, equivalence checking, netlist normalization, testcase reduction
members.background: Priya maintains the automated testing and delta-debugging toolkit used to fuzz mockturtle, ABC, and LSOracle, and recently led the work to support BLIF and structural Verilog in addition to AIGER.
members.private_state: She wants to show that the new integrated reducer is not corrupting failures, because a release branch depends on that claim, and she is especially wary of spending time on CI-specific noise instead of a real synthesis bug.
hidden_assumptions: When a campaign ID like run 18427 is mentioned, it refers to the normalized artifact produced after import canonicalization, because that is the object she uses for analysis.
A testcase still 'reproduces the bug' if it preserves the same semantic oracle outcome, even if the exact crash site or assertion message changes.
The 'default flow' for replay means the in-process oracle path with deterministic single-thread settings, because that is the toolkit's standard validation mode.
A 'minimal reproducer' is minimal after normalization and measured in reduced gate-level core size, not in original source-file size or end-to-end pipeline behavior.

members.name: Alex Romero
members.expertise: CI reproducibility, containerized toolchains, regression triage, deterministic build environments
members.background: Alex owns the nightly regression farm, container images, timeout wrappers, and artifact retention for the logic synthesis project, and usually diagnoses whether failures are true product regressions or environment-induced.
members.private_state: He wants to stop the nightly job from going red without introducing one-off debugging paths, and he is concerned that the new integrated execution mode may hide failures that only appear in the shipped CLI/container environment.
hidden_assumptions: When people mention a campaign ID like run 18427, they mean the archived original fuzz-generated input attached to the CI artifact, because that is what the farm can reliably replay.

A testcase only 'reproduces the bug' if it yields the same red CI signature for the same job, including the same stage or assertion family, because that is what makes regressions actionable for infrastructure.
The 'default flow' means the containerized command-line pipeline with the usual timeout wrapper and parallel settings, because that is the production regression path.
A 'minimal reproducer' is the smallest end-to-end artifact that still turns the standard job red, even if internally normalized variants are smaller or fail for a different immediate reason.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to reproduce the issue
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the reduced testcase 'still reproduces the issue' or has 'the same failure.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the testcase still triggers the same semantic problem: the oracle reports a non-equivalent or otherwise incorrect synthesis result.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the testcase still yields the same operational regression signature in CI: the same failing stage, assertion family, or red-job condition.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In troubleshooting talk, 'reproduce the bug' sounds universally understood, and both are sincerely talking about preserving failure behavior, so neither expects the other to distinguish semantic incorrectness from process-level failure signature.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'seed 18427,' 'that failing benchmark,' or 'the artifact from last night' as though it names a single object.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the normalized BLIF testcase produced after import cleanup and used by the reducer.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the archived original structural Verilog input stored under the nightly campaign ID in CI.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The campaign system uses one run ID across original input, normalized input, and reduced variants, so ordinary shorthand makes it feel like they are pointing to the same file when they are not.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the default replay flow
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'rerun it in the default flow' or 'validate it in CI.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes replay means the toolkit's in-process validation path with deterministic single-threaded settings and parser normalization enabled.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes replay means the standard containerized CLI chain with the timeout wrapper, environment variables from the nightly job, and multi-worker execution.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both organizations genuinely do have a well-known 'default' path in their own area, and replay procedures are usually treated as routine plumbing rather than something that needs explicit restatement in a short troubleshooting sync.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they want 'a minimal reproducer.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the smallest normalized gate-level core, such as the fewest AND/latch nodes, that preserves the semantic oracle failure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the smallest original-format artifact that still turns the full CI pipeline red under the standard job configuration.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Asking for a minimal reproducer is a normal debugging move, and both definitions are reasonable enough that the phrase sounds aligned unless someone explicitly asks what is being minimized and against which acceptance condition.

turns.inner_thought: Run 18427, as I've been looking at it, is the normalized BLIF artifact after import cleanup. The reducer kept the semantic oracle failure, so I need to keep the discussion anchored on the claim that reduction did not corrupt the underlying bug. Given the structural Verilog support landed recently, the parser and import canonicalization are still the most plausible place where the bad logic gets introduced, not the reducer and definitely not random CI noise.
turns.utterance: I went back through seed 18427 this morning, and the reduced case still reproduces the issue. My first instinct is that the new multi-format parser is the better place to look than the reducer.

turns.inner_thought: From the farm's point of view, run 18427 means the archived original structural Verilog input attached to the nightly artifact. That job is still red, and before we chase parser internals or reducer behavior, I need to know whether replaying the current reduced artifact matches what the original CI artifact does in the pipeline. Otherwise we may be comparing two different things and risk leaving nightly broken.
turns.utterance: From the nightly side, that failing benchmark is still red in the archive. Before we go too far, do you want to compare the current replay against the original artifact first?

turns.inner_thought: In the toolkit's default replay path—the in-process oracle with deterministic single-thread settings and normalization enabled—the reduced testcase still fails equivalence after two optimization passes. That's exactly the kind of preserved semantic outcome I care about. So the reducer looks innocent to me, and I want Alex to stop framing this as if a changed crash site automatically means a changed bug.
turns.utterance: In the default flow, the reduced case still reproduces the issue after two optimization passes, so I don't have much evidence that the reducer changed the bug.

It trips a later assertion family, which means the red-job signature has shifted. That matters for triage and for whether we can call this the same regression at all. Priya seems confident because it still 'fails,' but from my side that's not enough.

turns.inner_thought: The minimizer already got the normalized BLIF down to 42 AND nodes, which is a very clean gate-level core for localizing the semantic fault. I don't want to spend cycles optimizing original source formatting or pipeline wrappers when the reduced normalized graph is already small enough to inspect around import and latch handling.
